text: Priority is not earned — broker not yet enabled, hugin_rate not dogfooded; next move is orch-v1 enablement, not a new telemetry MCP
Plan duplicates the unfinished hugin_rate feedback loop without proving a gap that hugin_rate cannot fill
resource_assessment claim ('direct routing signal with no inference needed') is not defensible — calibration by model family, task type, and prompt wording is still required
SDK executor injection only covers Claude tasks, not Ollama, OpenRouter, Codex spawn, or pi-harness — mismatches the stated multi-runtime comparison goal
Model-authored events written with Classification:internal without provenance tags violates the trust model established elsewhere in the codebase
'No new infrastructure' claim overstated — new MCP entrypoint, bin, schema, report script, and SDK executor changes are real build and operational cost
Degradation under partial failure is a placeholder, not a policy — Munin write failures can add latency, trigger model retries, or create survivorship bias
Aggregation lacks denominators — friction rate cannot be computed from signals/friction/* alone; requires join against all tasks including zero-friction tasks
would_benefit_from uses cheap/mid/frontier/local-large — not the router's vocabulary (tiny/medium/large-reasoning/pi-large-coder); cannot drive actual routing decisions
Success criteria too weak — 'tool writes to Munin' is an implementation milestone, not a product outcome; needs correlation gates against hugin_rate
Self-review findings (calibration bias, schema versioning, retention, failure semantics, tool description) not absorbed into the plan snapshot
Response still anchors on friction-mcp as the likely destination before evidence exists — needs explicit kill criteria, not just promotion criteria
SDK injection defense confused about active path — orch-v1 broker worker routes through OpenRouter, not Claude Agent SDK; injection would miss the very corpus needed for baseline

Observer identity ambiguity — evaluator annotation (orchestrating Claude reviewing output) and delegate self-report (executing model mid-task) are different data with opposite potential biases; plan collapses them
20-30 task sample is too small to prove routing value across task types, aliases, runtime rows, and model families — anecdotes will masquerade as evidence
Lossy telemetry correction solves Munin coupling but not behavior coupling — giving the executing model an extra tool changes task behavior regardless of write success
